HW overlays stay disabled everywhere until reboot.
Turns on automatically when you open an app from the list.
The accessibility service is off, so Limpid cannot see which app is open.
Limpid only reads which app is in the foreground, to turn the video fix on for the apps you selected. It does not read screen content or what you type.

string-array.name: steps
string-array.item: Install Shizuku (F-Droid, GitHub or Google Play).
Enable Developer options: Settings → About phone → Software information → tap Build number 7 times.
In Shizuku: Start via Wireless debugging → Pairing. Samsung closes the pairing dialog when you switch apps, so use split screen or Shizuku\'s notification to type the code.
In Shizuku settings, turn on Start on boot, so it comes back after a reboot while on Wi-Fi.
Back in Limpid: Allow Limpid in Shizuku, then pick a mode.

resources.string: After a reboot the flag resets. As soon as Shizuku is running again, it wakes Limpid up and the saved mode is applied automatically. No other action is needed.

On some Samsung phones with One UI, apps like Facebook play videos with a gray, washed-out haze when the display controller composes the screen (hardware overlays). The video looks right as soon as any system overlay appears, like the volume panel. Disabling HW overlays moves composition to the GPU, so colors are always correct. It is the same switch as Developer options → Disable HW overlays, but applied automatically.
With the fix on, the GPU composes every frame. On a static screen the difference is negligible, but video and scrolling cost a bit more. That is why “Only for selected apps” is recommended.
On Android 13+, apps installed from a downloaded APK need: Settings → Apps → Limpid → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings. Or use “Enable automatically” on the main screen once Shizuku is ready.
Run it once with Developer options → Disable HW overlays OFF, then once with it ON, and send both results. This shows how One UI implements the switch.
